newsitem.title: USA: NEES proposes New England-Long Island link.
newsitem.headline: NEES proposes New England-Long Island link.

text.p: New England Electric System is proposing to develop a 600-megawatt high-voltage, direct current submarine cable transmission connection between Connecticut and Long Island, the utility holding company said.
The current cost estimate is $200 million, NEES said, adding it is working with ABB Group to provide the necessary equipment.
The proposed cable would run under Long Island Sound, connecting United Illuminating Co's East Shore substation in New Haven, Conn., to Long Island Lighting Co's Shoreham substation in Shoreham, N.Y.
The cable would be about 25 miles in length, NEES said, adding it would have minimal environmental impact and require no new land takings.
The company said the new transmission system or 'energy bridge' would introduce competitively attractive sources of power onto Long Island.

NEES is studying the proposal as a new business venture, project manager Dan Lorden told Reuters, pointing out the company's experience operating high-voltage, direct current transmission systems linking New England with Canada.
The Long Island Cable Project would use an independent transmission project model that allocates costs, risks, and benefits to owners and users of the cable, NEES said.
The company said it plans to solicit potential users to support the project through its permitting phase, and would build, operate, and maintain facilities for a fixed price.
"We'd be the bridge builders, toll collectors," Lorden explained.
"We have met with various stakeholders, public and regulatory officials, and environmental agencies to explain the project and garner support," Lorden said.
"Initial reactions to the project have been very favorable," he continued.

"We will conduct a solicitation of interest to support the project's permitting costs in March 1997. If successful, NEES would complete permitting, including regulatory approvals, by the end of 1998."
The project's planned in-service date is June 2000, the company said.

Users that support the development of the project would have the first right to enter into firm transmission service agreements for their share of the project's transmission capacity under accepted Federal Energy Regulatory Commission tariffs, NEES pointed out.
